review.note: Reviewed after the original review with its method. Six phases from the solve: the load rose 25 mm for 99.8 mm of fall (3.99, the slight fleet of the parts), and the sheaves turned in the ratio 1:2:3:4 from the dead end toward the fall. The 4:1 could only be read from numbers. Decided: the fall is the input (it was the block spacing); a longer stroke, 160 mm of fall for 40.1 mm of rise; equal-time ticks on the hook and on the fall end so their 4:1 spacing shows side by side; one index mark per sheave so the 1:2:3:4 rates can be seen; the block spacing as a dimension.

joints.note: upper span runs onto the driver (counter-clockwise): tight side; lower span slack

params.note: centre distance for 87 teeth on the pitch path

review.note: Reviewed after the original review with its method. Six phases from the solve: the driven pulley turns 180° per driver turn, the same way, with the belt teeth carried in the grooves; the numbers in the relations were for 60 and 120 mm pulleys at 200 mm, not the built 24 and 48 groove pulleys. The principle (one belt speed at both rims) had nothing to show it. Decided: keep the open timing belt; trace a pitch-circle point on each pulley with equal-time ticks, so each tick is the same 16 mm of rim on both pulleys while the turns are 30° and 15°; one index mark per pulley to count 2:1; tight and slack spans and the wrap angle drawn; the relations restated for the built pulleys.

edit.build.defining_relations: theta2 = (z1/z2) theta1 = theta1 / 2 for the open belt, both turning the same way; a crossed belt reverses the output. HTD 8M pitch diameters d = z p / pi = 61.1 and 122.2 mm. Open belt length L = 2 C cos(beta) + (pi - 2 beta) d1/2 + (pi + 2 beta) d2/2 with beta = asin((d2 - d1)/(2C)); 87 teeth (696 mm) give C = 201.7 mm and beta = 8.7°; small wrap angle 180° - 2 beta = 162.6°. For a friction belt the tension ratio T1/T2 <= e^(mu theta); power = (T1 - T2) v.
edit.build.range: driver 360° continuous; driven turns 180° per driver turn, the same way

joints.note: upper span runs onto the driver (counter-clockwise): tight side; lower span slack

params.note: chain length in pitches (even, no offset link)

review.note: Reviewed after the original review with its method. Six phases from the solve: the driven sprocket turns 180° per driver turn, the same way, and the rollers seat in every gap; but the chain ran on the pitch circles, so the chordal action the text explains (and the record's output character, Non-uniform) was absent from the motion. Decided: the chain is solved on the pitch polygon, so the chain speed falls to 0.978 of its peak once per tooth (2.2% for 15 teeth) and the speed plot shows the ripple the record promises; the pitch chord of the driver drawn; equal-time ticks on a pitch point of each sprocket and an index mark on each to count 2:1; the relations corrected to the built centre distance (62 links give 248.5 mm, not 254).

claims.text: chordal speed variation = 1 - cos(180°/z1) = 2.2% for 15 teeth

edit.build.defining_relations: theta2 = (z1/z2) theta1 on average, theta1 / 2 here; pitch diameter D = p / sin(180°/z) = 61.1 and 121.5 mm; links N = 2C/p + (z1+z2)/2 + ((z2-z1)/(2 pi))^2 p/C, so 62 links (even, no offset link) give C = 248.5 mm; chordal speed variation of the chain = 1 - cos(180°/z1) = 2.2% for 15 teeth, once per tooth.

review.note: Reviewed after the original review with its method. Six phases from the solve: the wheel turns at R / rw of the disc (3.0 at R 90, still at the centre, -1.0 at R -30), which matches the text; but the contact radius swept by itself over the cycle, so no setting could be held and the ratio was mixed with the shift. Decided: the contact radius R is a control (default 60, 2.0x), with ghost tread traces at R 30 (1:1) and R -30 (reverse); the contact circle on the disc and R as a dimension; the speed ratio plotted against R as the record asks.

claims.text: R = 60 turns the wheel at 2.0 x disc speed

edit.explain.motion: The input turns a flat disc. A wheel with a rubber or fibre rim presses on the disc face and can slide along its own shaft, which runs across the disc. Near the centre the wheel turns slowly, far out it turns fast, and moving it past the centre reverses it.
edit.build.range: disc continuous; contact radius R set from -30 to 90 mm: 15 to 90 gives 0.5 to 3.0 x disc speed, the centre stops the wheel, R -30 reverses it at 1.0 x

review.note: Reviewed after the original review with its method. Six phases from the solve: the lever rocks ±2° about the neck centre and the stiffness is 12,984 N·mm/rad, as the text says; but on the 60 mm lever the tip moved only ±2.1 mm, so the six phases looked almost the same. Decided: keep the true metal angle (a few degrees is part of the lesson, and K1 forbids exaggerating it); lengthen the lever to 100 mm so the tip moves ±3.5 mm; trace the tip on its arc; draw the neck's bend; and a 6x detail view of the neck where the bending happens. Rebuild (R7): the neck's bend is drawn as a signed arc with its angle (the bend overlay), the neck itself rigid either side of its centre (D9); the drive is a crank and slotted yoke under the base through a pin in the lever's tip.

edit.build.range: lever rocks ±2°; tip moves ±3.5 mm (lever 100 mm)

review.note: Reviewed after the original review with its method. Six phases from the solve: the shuttle holds near +7 mm, follows the pusher down to y = 3.43 mm (just past the 4.09 N force peak at 3.99 mm) and snaps 10 mm ahead of it to the far branch, then back the same way; that reads well. But the snap took 8° of the cycle, gone in a blink, and the pusher's 1 mm overshoot left the shuttle at ±7.01 mm instead of the stable ±6.95. Decided: the pusher's stroke ends at the stable states, so the shuttle comes to rest at ±6.95 mm with the springs unloaded; a time map slows the snap; ticks on the shuttle's path show the jump; the unstable centre line and the beam chords drawn. Rebuild (R7): the beams are drawn as their pseudo-rigid halves, rigid either side of each flexure (D9), with the bend on the overlays; the springs either side of the pusher's roller are drawn stretched between the roller and the window's ends; both snaps are slowed by the time map (spans).

claims.text: shuttle travels from +6.95 mm to -6.95 mm

edit.build.range: shuttle travels from +6.95 mm to -6.95 mm; pushed through two springs, it snaps ahead of the pusher at y = ±3.43 mm, just past the force peak at ±3.99 mm
edit.topology.notes: pseudo-rigid-body model: ground, shuttle, and two beams each split into two telescoping parts with an axial spring; flex ends as flexure pivots. The shuttle rides the pusher's roller in its window between two springs. Mobility counted from the joints is 2: the pusher is the one drive, and the shuttle's place along the window is set by the balance of the springs and the beams, which gives the snap. Real part is one piece

shape.note: base with the screw's two pillow blocks and the guide rail for the nut's flag

review.note: Unbuilt; reviewed against the record. The relation is exact and linear (3 mm per turn), but the record's 200 mm stroke takes 66.7 turns, and a screw turning one way cannot repeat its cycle. Decided: the screw turns 10 turns out and back, so the nut travels 30 mm, one lead per turn, with a tick on the nut's path at each turn; a mark on the handwheel to count turns; the guide that keeps the nut from turning is part of the lesson and stays in view; a section through the nut on the screw axis shows the loaded thread flank, the inclined plane of the text. Tr12x3 is kept: lead angle 5.2° against a friction angle of 8.5°, so it is self-locking. Rebuild (R7): the input is a reversing belt drive to the screw's end; the nut's ticks count the turns, so the handwheel mark is not kept.

claims.text: 10 turns move the nut 30 mm, one 3 mm lead per turn

edit.build.range: screw turned 10 turns (3600°) out and back; the nut travels 30 mm, one 3 mm lead per turn, linear and proportional. The full 200 mm stroke takes 66.7 turns
edit.topology.notes: ground, screw (revolute in end bearings), nut (prismatic on a guide); screw to nut is a helical (screw) pair. Overconstrained: the bearings, the guide and the thread share one axis, so the joint count gives -3 while the mechanism moves with 1; the coaxial pairs are redundant, not locking

shape.note: base with the screw's two pillow blocks and the guide rail for the nut's flag

params.note: the ball centres' share of the screw's turn relative to the nut: (1 - db cos(alpha) / dpw) / 2

review.note: Unbuilt; reviewed against the record. A turn moves the nut one 5 mm lead; the record's 300 mm in 60 turns cannot show in one repeating cycle. The principle, balls rolling between the grooves and recirculating, lives inside the nut. Decided: the screw turns 6 turns out and back (nut 30 mm, a tick per turn); a section through the nut on the screw axis is the teaching view, with the loaded balls, the groove walls and the return path highlighted; the balls circulate at 0.43 of the screw's turn relative to the nut (rolling between a turning and a still groove), which the text's 'about half' now states exactly; the return type is a design choice. Rebuild (R7): the return type is not offered as a control, because it changes the built nut; the tube return is built.

claims.text: 6 turns move the nut 30 mm, one 5 mm lead per turn

edit.build.range: screw turned 6 turns (2160°) out and back; the nut travels 30 mm, one 5 mm lead per turn, linear and proportional. The full 300 mm stroke takes 60 turns
edit.build.defining_relations: x = l theta / 360; drive torque T = F l / (2 pi eta); backdrive torque T = F l eta' / (2 pi) with eta' about 0.8; the balls roll between the turning screw groove and the still nut groove, so relative to the nut each ball centre turns at (1 - db cos(alpha) / dpw) / 2 = 0.43 of the screw's turn (db 3.175, dpw 16.6, alpha 45°) and advances 0.43 lead per screw turn before it recirculates.
edit.topology.notes: ground, screw, nut; the ball train is a rolling screw pair, its balls carried round the circuit and not separate kinematic links. Overconstrained: the bearings, the guide and the ball screw share one axis, so the joint count gives -3 while the mechanism moves with 1

params.note: pitch of the thread in the fixed nut (Tr24x5)
pitch of the thread in the moving nut (Tr20x4)

review.note: Unbuilt; reviewed against the record. With 1.0 and 0.8 mm pitches the nut moves 0.2 mm per turn: nothing would show, and the record's own note asked to exaggerate the drawing, which K1 forbids. Decided: real coarse threads of 5 and 4 mm (Tr24x5 in the fixed nut, Tr20x4 for the moving nut), the same 5:1 as the fine pair, so over 10 turns out and back the screw advances 50 mm and the nut 10 mm, both at true size; ticks once per turn on the screw's end and on the nut so 5 mm against 1 mm per turn reads; a same or opposite hand switch with the opposite-hand nut path (9 mm per turn) as a ghost; a section through both nuts shows the two pitches engaged. Rebuild (R7): the hand switch is not offered as a control, because the threads are built right hand and a control cannot change built parts; the opposite-hand nut path stays as a ghost. The screw advances through its fixed nut, so it is turned by a knob on its end, not belted.

claims.text: 10 turns move the nut 10 mm, p1 - p2 = 1 mm per turn

edit.ratio.typical: travel = p1 - p2 per turn: 5 - 4 = 1 mm per turn here; fine instrument pairs such as 1.0 - 0.8 = 0.2 mm per turn
edit.build.range: knob 3600° (10 turns) out and back; screw moves 50 mm, nut moves 10 mm (90 mm with opposite hands)
edit.build.notes: Show both motions: the screw visibly advancing through the fixed nut and the moving nut creeping slowly. The pitches are 5 and 4 mm (Tr24x5 and Tr20x4) so both motions read at true size: 5 mm and 1 mm per turn, the same 5:1 as an instrument pair of 1.0 and 0.8 mm. A design switch sets same or opposite hands; opposite hands make a compound screw, 9 mm per turn.
edit.topology.notes: ground with fixed nut, screw with two threads, sliding nut on a guide; two screw (helical) pairs plus one prismatic guide. Overconstrained: the two threads and the guide share one axis, so the joint count gives -3 while the mechanism moves with 1

review.note: Unbuilt; reviewed against the record. The relations hold: with the belt length fixed at 582.7 mm, r1 from 25 to 62.07 mm takes r2 from 62.07 to 25 mm and the output from 0.40 to 2.48 x the input (spread 6.2), for a sheave shift of 14.4 mm. Decided (issue): the ratio is a control, the input pitch radius r1, never swept by itself; default r1 = 30 mm (r2 58.3 mm, output 0.515 x) so the two pulleys differ at a glance; ghost traces of the output mark at both limits; the principle is the sheaves closing and opening, which shows edge-on, so a section through both shaft axes is the teaching view with the movable sheaves and the belt highlighted; the movable sheaves sit on opposite sides so the belt stays in line.

claims.text: r1 = 30 mm gives the output 0.515 x the input

edit.topology.notes: ground, input shaft with fixed sheave, input movable sheave, output shaft with fixed sheave, output movable sheave; the belt joins the two shafts. Movable sheaves slide on splines on opposite sides. Mobility counted from the joints is 3: the input sheave's slide is the ratio setting, a second controlled freedom, and the output sheave's slide follows from the fixed belt length; the drive is one

review.note: Unbuilt; reviewed against the record. The output speed is x / rc times the disc's, so with a fixed carriage it is only a variable-ratio drive; the integral shows only when x changes while the disc turns. Decided (issue): two drivers, the disc and the carriage; by default the carriage follows x = 40 sin(disc angle), so the output winds up to 305.6° and back once per disc turn, plotted together with x (the integrand and its integral); output speed up to 2.67 x, reversing as the ball crosses the centre; the cylinder sits 45° up and across from the ball so the ball and both contacts stay visible from above; x is drawn as a dimension from the disc axis.

edit.build.range: disc continuous; carriage follows x = 40 sin(disc angle) from -40 to +40 mm by default; output turns either way at up to 2.67 x disc speed (3.3 x at the full 50 mm) and swings 0 to 305.6° and back each disc turn
edit.topology.notes: ground, disc, carriage, ball, output cylinder; ball rolls on disc and cylinder and is held in the carriage cage. Mobility counted from the joints is 4: the two drives (disc and carriage), and the two rolling contacts counted as plain contacts; with no slip they set the cylinder's turn and the ball's, leaving only the ball's idle spin about the line through its contacts
